name: Move Tool
description: Drags layers, selections and guides around the canvas, and doubles as the hub for aligning and distributing layers via the options bar. The first tool architects reach for when repositioning trees, people and other entourage in a render collage.

name: Artboard Tool
description: Creates and resizes artboards so several presentation boards or drawing sheets can live in one document. Handy for laying out a portfolio spread or a set of diagram variants side by side.

name: Rectangular Marquee Tool
description: Draws rectangular pixel selections; hold Shift for a square. Useful for isolating a facade bay or cropping a clean strip of sky before adjustment.

name: Elliptical Marquee Tool
description: Draws oval and circular selections; hold Shift to constrain to a circle. Reached for when masking round elements such as sun discs, vignettes or circular diagram callouts.

name: Lasso Tool
description: Freehand selection tool for quickly ringing an irregular area. Good for rough masks around foliage or loose regions you intend to refine or feather afterwards.

name: Polygonal Lasso Tool
description: Builds a selection from straight-edged clicks, which suits the hard geometry of buildings. The go-to for cutting a facade or roofline cleanly out of a photograph.

name: Magnetic Lasso Tool
description: Snaps a selection edge to contrast boundaries as you trace, useful where a building meets sky. Works best on clean, high-contrast edges; noisy textures may need manual clicks.

name: Object Selection Tool
description: Drag a rough box around an object and Photoshop finds its edges automatically. A fast way to isolate a person, tree or vehicle for masking into a render.

name: Quick Selection Tool
description: Paints a selection that grows along similar tones and edges as you drag. Useful for grabbing large coherent areas such as a lawn, a wall plane or a stretch of paving.

name: Magic Wand Tool
description: Selects contiguous pixels of similar colour in one click, controlled by a tolerance value. Ideal for lifting flat-colour areas out of exported CAD elevations or diagram fills.

name: Crop Tool
description: Trims or extends the canvas, with ratio presets, overlay guides and straightening built in. Essential for composing final render crops to a consistent board format.

name: Perspective Crop Tool
description: Crops while remapping a skewed plane to a straight-on rectangle. Perfect for rectifying photographs of drawings, site boards or facades shot at an angle.

name: Frame Tool
description: Draws rectangular or elliptical placeholder frames that images drop into and auto-mask, much like InDesign frames. Useful for building portfolio board templates directly in Photoshop.

name: Eyedropper Tool
description: Samples a colour from the canvas into the foreground swatch. Reach for it when matching material tones across a render or picking a palette from a reference photograph.

name: Ruler Tool
description: Measures distances and angles on the canvas and can straighten a tilted layer from the options bar. Useful for checking proportions or levelling a skewed site photograph.

name: Spot Healing Brush Tool
description: Removes small blemishes in one dab by sampling the surroundings automatically. The quickest fix for sensor dust, stray cables or minor render artefacts.

name: Healing Brush Tool
description: Paints with texture from an Alt-clicked source point while blending tone and lighting from the destination. Gives more control than the spot version when repairing brick, render or concrete textures.

name: Patch Tool
description: Drag a selected problem area onto clean texture and Photoshop blends the repair in. Efficient for erasing large distractions such as skips, signage or parked cars from site photographs.

name: Remove Tool
description: Brush over an unwanted object and machine learning reconstructs the background behind it. Faster than manual cloning for clearing wires, bins and people from context photographs.

name: Content-Aware Move Tool
description: Moves a selected object to a new position while filling the hole it leaves and blending it into its new surroundings. Useful for nudging entourage or street furniture to improve a composition.

name: Brush Tool
description: The core painting tool, with pressure-sensitive size and opacity control. Architects use it constantly for painting layer masks, adding shadow washes and hand-rendered texture over line drawings.

name: Pencil Tool
description: Paints hard-edged, aliased strokes with no soft falloff. Suits crisp pixel-precise work such as tidying exported linework or drawing on very low-resolution diagrams.

name: Mixer Brush Tool
description: Blends colours on the canvas like wet paint, mixing what is already there with the loaded colour. Used for painterly render overpainting and softening harsh CG material transitions.

name: Clone Stamp Tool
description: Paints an exact copy of pixels from an Alt-clicked source point. The classic tool for extending brick coursing, duplicating window bays or patching texture where healing tools blend too much.

name: History Brush Tool
description: Paints a chosen earlier history state back into the image. Lets you apply a filter or adjustment globally, then brush it away selectively - for example restoring sharpness only on the building.

name: Eraser Tool
description: Deletes pixels from a layer, or paints the background colour on a locked Background layer. On masked workflows it is often better to paint the mask instead, keeping edits reversible.

name: Background Eraser Tool
description: Erases sampled colours under the brush centre while protecting differing edge colours, leaving transparency. Occasionally useful for stripping sky from behind complex roof silhouettes.

name: Gradient Tool
description: Drags a smooth blend between colours or transparency, now applied as an editable on-canvas gradient. Constantly used for graded skies, ground-plane fades and atmospheric depth in render post-production.

name: Paint Bucket Tool
description: Fills contiguous areas of similar colour with the foreground colour or a pattern. Quick for blocking flat colour into diagram regions or exported plan drawings.

name: Blur Tool
description: Softens pixels locally as you brush. Handy for knocking back a distracting background detail or easing a hard cut-out edge without touching the whole layer.

name: Sharpen Tool
description: Increases local contrast under the brush to crisp up detail. Useful for selectively emphasising material texture or foreground edges in a render without global sharpening.

name: Smudge Tool
description: Pushes pixels around as if dragging a finger through wet paint. Occasionally used to pull wisps into skies or blend painted entourage edges into a scene.

name: Dodge Tool
description: Brightens the area you brush, with separate control over shadows, midtones and highlights. Used to lift light onto facades, pick out sunlit surfaces and add sparkle to glazing.

name: Burn Tool
description: Darkens the brushed area, targeting shadows, midtones or highlights. The natural partner to dodging for grounding objects with contact shadows and deepening recesses in a render.

name: Sponge Tool
description: Saturates or desaturates colour locally as you brush. Useful for calming an over-vivid car or sign that competes with the architecture in a visual.

name: Pen Tool
description: Draws precise vector paths with bezier handles, convertible to selections, masks or shapes. The most accurate way to cut out hard-edged architecture for compositing.

name: Freeform Pen Tool
description: Draws a path freehand and fits anchor points to your stroke, with an optional magnetic mode. A looser alternative to the Pen for organic outlines such as tree canopies.

name: Curvature Pen Tool
description: Places points and fits smooth curves through them automatically, no handle-dragging required. An easier entry to path drawing when tracing arches, curved roofs or road edges.

name: Horizontal Type Tool
description: Creates point or paragraph text as an editable type layer. Used for titling boards, labelling diagrams and annotating renders before export.

name: Path Selection Tool
description: Selects and moves whole paths or shape components. Used when repositioning vector callouts, cut-out paths or shape-layer elements on a board.

name: Direct Selection Tool
description: Selects individual anchor points and handles so you can reshape a path after drawing it. Essential for refining a Pen cut-out around tricky architectural details.

name: Rectangle Tool
description: Draws rectangular vector shapes with live corner radius controls. Useful for diagram frames, colour blocks and masking panels on presentation boards.

name: Ellipse Tool
description: Draws elliptical and circular vector shapes. Reached for when adding key-plan markers, bubble diagrams or circular crops to a layout.

name: Line Tool
description: Draws straight vector lines with adjustable weight and optional arrowheads. Ideal for leader lines, section markers and dimension-style callouts over images.

name: Custom Shape Tool
description: Stamps predefined vector shapes, including arrows and symbols, from a shape library. A quick source of north arrows and diagram glyphs without leaving Photoshop.

name: Hand Tool
description: Pans the view around a zoomed-in image; hold the spacebar to invoke it temporarily from any tool. Constant companion when retouching large renders at pixel level.

name: Rotate View Tool
description: Rotates the on-screen view non-destructively, like turning a sheet of paper, without altering pixels. Useful when painting masks or strokes at a comfortable wrist angle.

name: Zoom Tool
description: Zooms in with a click or scrubby drag; hold Alt to zoom out. Fundamental for flipping between whole-image composition checks and pixel-level retouching.

name: Default Foreground and Background Colours
description: Resets the swatches to black foreground over white background. Worth pressing before mask work so you know exactly which tone the brush will paint.

name: Switch Foreground and Background Colours
description: Swaps the foreground and background swatches. Used constantly while painting layer masks to flip between concealing with black and revealing with white.

name: Decrease/Increase Brush Size
description: The square-bracket keys shrink or enlarge the current brush tip; add Shift to change hardness. Keeps mask painting fluid without visiting the brush picker.

name: Quick Mask Mode
description: Toggles a mode where you paint a selection as a red overlay with any brush, then exit to convert it into marching ants. A forgiving way to build soft, painterly selections for atmospheric adjustments.

name: Cycle Screen Modes
description: Cycles between standard, full screen with menu bar and full screen views. Useful for judging a finished render against a clean neutral surround before presenting.

name: New Layer
description: Creates an empty layer above the current one, with options for name, blend mode and opacity. Disciplined layer-making is the backbone of a non-destructive render post-production file.

name: New Layer via Copy
description: Copies the current selection, or the whole layer if nothing is selected, onto a fresh layer. The reflex move before any risky edit, and the fastest way to duplicate an element for arraying entourage.

name: New Layer via Cut
description: Moves the selected pixels onto their own layer, leaving a hole behind. Useful for separating a building from its background so each can be adjusted independently.

name: Duplicate Layer
description: Duplicates the active layer or group, optionally into another open document. Handy for carrying a graded sky or a set of adjustment layers between render files.

name: Group Layers
description: Collects the selected layers into a folder that can be moved, masked and blended as one. Keeping vegetation, people and sky in named groups keeps large visualisation files navigable.

name: Ungroup Layers
description: Dissolves the selected group, returning its layers to the main stack. Used when a grouping no longer reflects how you want to structure the file.

name: Merge Layers
description: Flattens the selected layers, or the layer into the one below, into a single layer. Reduces file weight once a passage of work is final, at the cost of later editability.

name: Merge Visible
description: Combines every visible layer into one, discarding hidden ones. Useful just before a final sharpen when you no longer need the layered structure.

name: Stamp Visible
description: Creates a new merged copy of everything visible while leaving all the original layers intact. The standard move before applying Camera Raw or sharpening to a finished composite without losing the stack.

name: Flatten Image
description: Collapses the entire document to a single Background layer. Only sensible on a copy destined for delivery, since all layered editability is lost.

name: Create Clipping Mask
description: Clips the current layer so it only shows where the layer below has pixels. Perfect for confining a texture, tone or adjustment to a single building cut-out.

name: Add Layer Mask
description: Attaches a greyscale mask to the layer: paint black to hide, white to reveal. The cornerstone of non-destructive compositing, from blending skies to fading materials on a facade study.

name: Add Vector Mask
description: Masks a layer with a resolution-independent path instead of pixels. Gives perfectly crisp edges for hard architectural cut-outs that may be rescaled later.

name: New Adjustment Layer
description: Adds an editable adjustment, such as Curves or Hue/Saturation, that affects all layers below without changing their pixels. The professional way to grade renders so every decision stays reversible.

name: New Fill Layer
description: Creates a layer filled with a solid colour, gradient or pattern, complete with its own mask. Ideal for tone washes, graded skies and consistent background colours across board sets.

name: Convert to Smart Object
description: Wraps a layer so transforms and filters apply non-destructively and the source can be re-edited. Place renders as smart objects so repeated scaling on a board never degrades them.

name: Rasterise Layer
description: Converts a type, shape or smart object layer into plain pixels. Needed before pixel-level painting or filters that refuse to run on vector or smart content.

name: Layer Opacity Keys
description: With a non-painting tool active, tapping a number key sets the layer opacity in ten-percent steps. A fast way to fade an overlay drawing over a photograph while tracing.

name: Cycle Blend Modes
description: Steps the active layer through blend modes one by one. Invaluable for auditioning how a shadow pass, texture or light glow sits over a render.

name: Set Blend Mode: Multiply
description: Jumps the layer straight to Multiply, which darkens by multiplying tones. The classic mode for laying line drawings or shadow passes over a base image with whites turning transparent.

name: Set Blend Mode: Screen
description: Sets the layer to Screen, which lightens by inverting and multiplying, making black transparent. Ideal for compositing glows, light fixtures and night-render highlights.

name: Lock Transparent Pixels
description: Locks the layer's transparency so painting only affects existing pixels. Lets you recolour a tree or figure cut-out without ever straying past its silhouette.

name: Select All Layers
description: Selects every layer in the panel at once. Useful before grouping an unruly file or transforming an entire board's contents together.

name: Bring to Front
description: Moves the active layer to the top of the stack. Used when foreground entourage or annotation must sit above everything else.

name: Bring Forward
description: Moves the active layer one step up the stack. A quick nudge when a person should stand in front of a bollard but behind a tree.

name: Send Backward
description: Moves the active layer one step down the stack. Useful for slotting new entourage behind existing foreground elements.

name: Send to Back
description: Drops the active layer to the bottom of the stack. Typically used for pushing a replacement sky behind every other element of a composite.

name: Align Layers
description: Aligns the selected layers by their edges or centres, also available from the Move Tool options bar. Keeps rows of images and captions ruler-straight on portfolio boards.

name: Distribute Layers
description: Spaces three or more selected layers evenly by edges or centres. The quickest way to set a run of thumbnails or diagram panels at equal intervals.

name: Layer Style: Drop Shadow
description: Adds an editable shadow effect behind the layer's content. Useful for lifting cut-out plans or photos off the page on a presentation board, or faking quick contact shadows.

name: Blending Options
description: Opens the layer style dialogue with advanced controls including Blend If sliders. Blend If is a hidden gem for dropping a texture only into the highlights or shadows of a render.

name: Copy Layer Style
description: Copies the active layer's effects so they can be pasted onto other layers. Keeps shadows and strokes consistent across every image frame on a board set.

name: Select All
description: Selects the entire canvas. Commonly the first step before Copy Merged when lifting a whole composite into another document.

name: Deselect
description: Drops the current selection so edits apply everywhere again. Worth pressing habitually - a forgotten selection is the classic reason an adjustment mysteriously does nothing.

name: Reselect
description: Restores the most recently dropped selection. A lifesaver when you deselect a painstaking building cut-out a moment too soon.

name: Inverse Selection
description: Flips the selection to cover everything that was not selected. Standard practice after selecting a sky: invert to work on the building instead.

name: Feather
description: Softens the selection edge by a pixel radius so subsequent edits fade out gently. Essential for blending tonal adjustments into a render without visible seams.

name: Expand Selection
description: Grows the selection outwards by a set number of pixels. Useful for closing tiny gaps around a cut-out before filling or deleting the background.

name: Contract Selection
description: Shrinks the selection inwards by a set number of pixels. Often used to pull a selection just inside a building edge so no background halo survives the cut-out.

name: Select Subject
description: Uses machine learning to select the most prominent subject in one click. A strong starting point for cutting people and objects out for render entourage, refined afterwards in Select and Mask.

name: Select Sky
description: Automatically selects the sky region of a photograph or render, including around fiddly tree lines. The usual first step before grading a sky or swapping it entirely.

name: Select and Mask
description: Opens a dedicated workspace for refining selection edges, with the Refine Hair brush for wispy detail. Where rough tree and figure selections become convincing, halo-free masks.

name: Colour Range
description: Builds a selection from sampled colours or tonal ranges such as highlights and shadows across the whole image. Useful for grabbing every patch of sky between leaves, or all the glazing on a facade at once.

name: Transform Selection
description: Scales, rotates or skews the selection boundary itself without touching any pixels. Handy for adapting one window selection to fit the next bay along a facade.

name: Save Selection
description: Stores the current selection as an alpha channel for later reuse. Worth doing for any laborious cut-out, so the building mask survives to the next working session.

name: Load Selection
description: Recalls a saved selection, or loads any layer or channel as one; Ctrl-clicking a layer thumbnail does the same. Brings a stored facade mask back instantly for further grading passes.

name: Copy Merged
description: Copies the selected area as it appears on screen, flattening all visible layers into the clipboard. The way to lift a finished detail from a layered composite into another document.

name: Paste in Place
description: Pastes clipboard content at its original coordinates rather than the view centre. Keeps elements perfectly registered when moving them between same-sized render iterations.

name: Paste Into
description: Pastes the clipboard inside the active selection, automatically creating a layer mask from it. A neat one-step way to drop a new sky into a selected sky region.

name: Fill
description: Fills the selection or layer with a colour, pattern or content-aware result; Alt+Backspace and Ctrl+Backspace fill with foreground or background colour directly. Everyday workhorse for backgrounds, masks and quick patch repairs.

name: Content-Aware Fill
description: Opens a workspace that synthesises new texture to fill the selection, with control over which areas it samples. The heavyweight option for removing large objects such as vehicles or scaffolding from site photography.

name: Stroke (Outline Selection)
description: Draws a coloured border along the current selection or layer edge at a chosen width. Useful for quickly outlining a highlighted zone on a plan or aerial photograph.

name: Levels
description: Remaps shadows, midtones and highlights with three sliders under a histogram. The quick tool for punching up a flat render export or cleaning grey backgrounds out of scanned sketches.

name: Curves
description: Adjusts tone and colour by reshaping a curve, offering the finest control of any adjustment. The core grading tool for render post-production, from gentle S-curve contrast to per-channel colour casts.

name: Hue/Saturation
description: Shifts hue, saturation and lightness globally or per colour range. Constantly used to retune grass greens, mute competing colours or test alternative material tints on a facade.

name: Black & White
description: Converts to monochrome with per-colour luminance sliders, so a blue sky can go moody-dark while brickwork stays light. Ideal for elegant greyscale portfolio imagery and massing studies.

name: Invert
description: Flips every tone to its negative. Most used on layer masks to reverse what is hidden, or to turn white-on-black CAD exports into black-on-white linework.

name: Shadows/Highlights
description: Recovers detail by lifting shadows and taming highlights independently, based on local context. Rescues site photographs where the building is silhouetted against a bright sky.

name: Vibrance
description: Boosts muted colours more than already-saturated ones, protecting skin tones. A safer general saturation lift for renders than the blunt Saturation slider.

name: Camera Raw Filter
description: Opens the full raw-processing toolset - exposure, colour grading, clarity, dehaze, optics - as a filter on any layer. Many visualisers run their entire final grade here on a stamped composite.

name: Free Transform
description: Scales, rotates, skews and distorts the layer or selection with on-screen handles; right-click for extra modes and hold Ctrl to drag corners freely. The everyday tool for fitting entourage and textures into a scene's perspective.

name: Transform Again
description: Repeats the last transform; add Alt to repeat onto a duplicate. Chaining duplicates with a fixed offset is a quick way to array balusters, lamp posts or facade modules.

name: Warp
description: Bends the layer over an editable grid with adjustable control points. Used to wrap a poster onto a curved hoarding or ease a texture around a rounded form.

name: Perspective Warp
description: Defines planes over an image then lets you reshape its perspective, straightening converging verticals or adjusting viewpoint. Tailor-made for correcting keystoning in architectural photography.

name: Content-Aware Scale
description: Rescales an image while protecting detected important content, stretching mainly the bland areas. Useful for widening a sky or foreground to fit a board format without distorting the building.

name: Puppet Warp
description: Pins a mesh over the layer so parts can be bent around fixed points. Handy for adjusting a cut-out figure's pose or curving a tree branch away from a facade.

name: Image Rotation
description: Rotates or flips the entire canvas, including by arbitrary angles. Used for squaring up scanned hand drawings before tracing or presentation.

name: Generative Fill
description: Fills a selection with AI-generated content from a text prompt, or seamlessly removes and replaces what was there. Increasingly used for quick context, foreground foliage or patching gaps in site photography - check outputs critically before client issue.

name: Generative Expand
description: Extends the canvas with the Crop Tool and lets AI invent plausible surroundings in the new space. Useful when a render is framed too tightly for the board proportion it must fill.

name: Sky Replacement
description: Swaps the sky for one from a library or your own image, automatically masking edges and relighting the foreground to match. A minutes-not-hours route to consistent skies across a set of visuals.

name: Last Filter
description: Re-applies the most recently used filter with the same settings. Speeds up repeating an identical blur or sharpen across several layers of a composite.

name: Gaussian Blur
description: Applies an even, controllable softening across the layer. A staple for atmospheric depth, soft shadows under entourage and knocking back backgrounds in diagrams.

name: Smart Sharpen
description: Sharpens with control over radius, noise reduction and separate shadow and highlight fading. The usual final-output sharpen for renders headed to print or portfolio.

name: Unsharp Mask
description: The classic edge-contrast sharpener with amount, radius and threshold controls. Still a dependable choice for crisping scanned drawings and lineweights.

name: High Pass
description: Isolates edge detail on a grey layer; set that layer to Overlay for precise, controllable sharpening. A favourite finishing trick because the effect can be masked or faded at will.

name: Blur Gallery
description: A set of on-canvas blur effects including Field Blur, Iris Blur and Tilt-Shift with placeable pins. Tilt-Shift is popular for giving aerial photographs and masterplan views a model-like depth of field.

name: Liquify
description: Opens a workspace for pushing, bulging and reshaping pixels with pressure-like brushes. Occasionally rescues a slightly wonky cut-out or reshapes foliage to frame a view better.

name: Vanishing Point
description: Lets you define perspective planes and then clone, paint and paste in correct foreshortening along them. Powerful for extending facades, paving or repeating window bays convincingly in perspective photographs.

name: New Document
description: Creates a document from presets or custom size, resolution and colour mode. Setting correct print resolution and dimensions here saves repeated grief at board printing time.

name: Save
description: Saves the working document, keeping layers when saved as PSD or TIFF. Save early and often - large render composites and crashes are old acquaintances.

name: Save As
description: Saves the document under a new name, location or format. Useful for versioning milestone states of a visual so earlier directions can be revisited.

name: Save a Copy
description: Writes a copy in formats such as JPEG or PNG while your layered working file stays open and untouched. The tidy way to issue a flattened review image mid-session.

name: Export As
description: Exports the document or individual artboards with format, scale and resampling options and a preview. The main route for issuing web-resolution versions of boards and visuals.

name: Quick Export as PNG
description: Exports the document or selected layers straight to PNG with no dialogue. Perfect for firing off a quick diagram or work-in-progress render to the project team.

name: Save for Web (Legacy)
description: The older export dialogue with fine control over compression, palette and file size preview. Still favoured when squeezing portfolio images under strict upload size limits.

name: Place Embedded
description: Imports an image or vector file as a smart object stored inside the document. The safe way to bring renders and logos onto a board so they can be rescaled without quality loss.

name: Place Linked
description: Imports a file as a smart object that stays linked to the original on disk, updating when it changes. Ideal when the same masterplan or key render appears across several board documents.

name: Image Size
description: Resamples or re-labels the image's pixel dimensions and print resolution. Where you check a render really will hold up at 300 ppi on an A1 board.

name: Canvas Size
description: Grows or trims the canvas around the existing image from a chosen anchor point. Used to add margin for titles or extend working space beyond a render's edge.

name: Zoom In
description: Steps the view magnification up. Paired with its opposite constantly while alternating between detail retouching and whole-image judgement.

name: Zoom Out
description: Steps the view magnification down. Zooming right out regularly is the best defence against over-retouching detail nobody will see at print size.

name: Fit on Screen
description: Zooms so the whole canvas fits the window. The instant reset after deep zoomed-in work on a large visual.

name: Actual Size
description: Displays the image at 100 percent, one image pixel per screen pixel. The honest zoom level for judging sharpness and noise before export.

name: Rulers
description: Toggles rulers along the canvas edges, from which guides can be dragged. First step in setting up margin and grid guides for a portfolio board.

name: Show Guides
description: Toggles visibility of ruler guides. Flick them off to judge the composition clean, back on to keep aligning.

name: New Guide Layout
description: Generates a full grid of guides from column, row, gutter and margin values. Builds a proper layout grid for presentation boards in seconds.

name: Snap
description: Toggles snapping to guides, grids and layer edges. Keep it on for board layout accuracy; switch it off when nudging pixels freely in a retouch.

name: Show Grid
description: Displays a customisable document-wide grid. Useful as a temporary armature when composing multi-image boards or checking proportions.

name: Extras
description: Hides or shows all non-printing helpers at once: guides, grids, selection edges and more. Best-known for temporarily hiding the marching ants while judging an edit inside a selection.

name: Undo
description: Steps backwards through recent edits, one per press. Combined with the History Panel it makes experimentation in render post-production essentially free.

name: Redo
description: Steps forward again through edits you have undone. Useful for flicking back and forth to compare before and after states of a grade.

name: History Panel
description: Lists recent states so you can jump back multiple steps or take snapshots to return to. Take a snapshot before a risky experiment on a deadline render.

name: Actions Panel
description: Records sequences of commands for one-click replay. Record your standard sharpen-and-export routine once and apply it to every visual in a set.

name: Batch
description: Runs a recorded action across a whole folder of files. The way to resize, watermark or grade forty competition images while you make coffee.

name: Character Panel
description: Controls typeface, size, tracking, leading and other type attributes for text layers. Where board titles and annotation labels get typographically consistent.

name: Preferences
description: Opens application settings covering performance, scratch disks, units and cursors. Setting units to millimetres and assigning a fast scratch disk pays off on large board files.

name: Colour Settings
description: Sets the working colour spaces and profile policies for the application. Getting sRGB versus Adobe RGB right here prevents prints and screen exports drifting from what you approved.
